correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed character orthogonality: the t multiplier enforces x dot y=1, with t unit producing q^(2n-2) times the unit Kloosterman sum, t in the nonzero socle producing q^(3n-2) times a field Kloosterman sum for socle frequencies, and t=0 contributing only at the origin. Square-zero unit-fibre stationary phase forces residue t^2=residue a dot b. In odd residue characteristic two stationary phases cannot cancel because generating characters have odd prime-power order; in even characteristic the stationary root is unique. The q-1 terms in the finite-field sum cannot cancel since q-1 is not divisible by the field characteristic. Counting nonzero residue a and prescribed dot-product fibres gives the exact rank, including q=2 and mixed characteristic. Finite exact cyclotomic enumeration over Z/4 and Z/9 for n=2 found ranks 112 and 2025 respectively; these do not prove all rings.

final_claim: For all finite commutative length-two chain rings and n>=2, the unnormalized additive Fourier transform of x dot y=1 survives exactly at socle frequency pairs and at primitive frequencies with nonzero-square residue dot product (all nonzero products in characteristic two); the convolution rank is q^(2n)[1+s_q(q^n-1)q^(n-1)].
limitations: Only length-two finite commutative chain rings, unit level, n>=2, additive complex convolution; not all quadratic shells or all eigenvalue multiplicities.
